For a player that is worth so much, especially financially, to an organization’s success, Guerrero’s down year has led to some vitriol from the Blue Jays’ fan base. And that’s likely to continue after hearing recent comments from the star infielder.
Guerrero, 27, sat down with Telemicro News recently, where he discussed his struggles at the plate this season, and how it reflects on his contract extension.
His comments were, well, interesting.
"The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I’m going to do," Guerrero said, as translated by MLB reporter Héctor Gómez. "I understand why the fans believe it’s the other way around. Sometimes, I think that way, too, like, ‘Oh, they give me this money, and I’m not doing enough,’ but you know I try my best, and I’m working hard.
"The fans, I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you. But when you are not at your best, not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."
After catching heat from Blue Jays fans, Guerrero was approached about the viral quotes, which he responded to.
"That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year," Guerrero said, via MLB.com. "I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn’t help my team get to the postseason. I said I felt – that it’s my personal opinion – that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.
"To the fans, I’ve never stopped working very hard. I am going to go into the offseason again to prepare myself the best I can. Physically, mentally, everything that I have like I always do for my team and my teammates."
In Guerrero’s defense, that is technically what the Blue Jays did when they dished out his 14-year, $500 million extension, which is only behind Shohei Ohtani’s 10-year, $700 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Juan Soto’s 15-year, $765 million deal with the New York Mets. The franchise paid Guerrero for what he did from his debut in 2019 up to a fantastic 2025 campaign, where he belted eight homers and hit .397 across 18 postseason games.
But these comments show that Guerrero mustn’t be aware of what putting pen to money-filled paper meant in April 2025. No longer is it time in any sport, let alone Major League Baseball, where contracts are dished out based solely on past performance. It’s looking ahead to the future, where those past performances are expected to continue through a much-more lucrative deal.
MLB franchises sign players to contracts based on the market, and that market is justified by how the player will perform for them later on, while obviously looking at the track record in the past.
With any investment, those dishing out the big bucks want a return.
So, in a season where the home run total for a slugger is less than double digits – he still has time to at least get to 10 – and a career-low WAR (albeit the 2020 COVID-shortened campaign) has been accumulated, the Blue Jays and its fan base have every right to be disappointed. Yes, Guerrero was a major reason why Toronto reached the World Series in 2025, but the team and its fans are also allowed to voice displeasure with not just a down year – a career-worst performance in various metrics.
Would the Mets have dished out the highest-paying contract in league history if they didn’t expect Soto to continue performing at his superstar pace? No.
Would the Dodgers have agreed to give Ohtani $700 million, with heavy deferrals, might we add, to pay him for years without helping them reach their World Series goals? No.
From Mike Trout, to Mookie Betts, to Aaron Judge and the list goes on, every franchise wants to see a player they sign, especially for nine figures, to pay dividends. That’s the reality of the situation, whether Guerrero wants to view his deal as what he’s done in the past.
This is just one season, but Guerrero’s outlook needs to change just as much as his production moving forward on the remaining 13 years of his deal.

item.content:encoded:
You won't find many people who disagree with the statement that Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is having a disappointing 2026 season. In fact, they may have words even more harsh for a first baseman with only one home run at his home ballpark this year.
Through 141 games, Guerrero is slashing .263/.336/.359, with an OPS that ranks 23rd out of 26 qualified first basemen in MLB. He is doing this in the first season of a 14-year, $500 million contract that ranks as the third-largest in league history by guaranteed money.
Guerrero's underperformance looms large for a Blue Jays team that will miss the playoffs a year after reaching the World Series, especially looking forward given how much the franchise has invested in him. Which is why a recent comment made in a Spanish-language interview with Telemicro News didn't go down so well.
Guerrero's answer to a question about this season, translated by Héctor Gómez:
"The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I'm going to do. I understand why the fans believe it's the other way around. Sometimes I think that way too, like 'Oh they give me this money and I'm not doing enough,' but you know I try my best and I'm working hard.
The fans I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you but when you are not at your best not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."
For those unfamiliar with the economics of sports teams, paying a player for past performance rather than what they will do — as Guerrero said the Blue Jays did — is the exact opposite of what front offices are supposed to do. If it worked the way Guerrero is suggesting, his teammate Max Scherzer would probably be guaranteed more than $3 million this season.
The statement went viral, with one thread on the Blue Jays subreddit getting more than 300 comments in less than three hours. They, largely, are not happy.
Guerrero, or the Blue Jays, apparently felt the heat enough that he spoke to reporters hours after the comment started circulating and attempted to give a better answer. His response, via Keegan Matheson of MLB.com:
"That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year. I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn't help my team get to the postseason. I said I felt — that it's my personal opinion — that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.
"To the fans, I've never stopped working very hard. I am going to go into the offseason again to prepare myself the best I can. Physically, mentally, everything that I have like I always do for my team and my teammates."
That's a bit better, but Guerrero actually doubles down on the idea that players are paid for past performance and tries to note that he signed his megadeal at the beginning of the 2025 season. It did not go into effect until this year, though, as Guerrero played out 2025 on his $28.5 million arbitration salary.
When asked, Guerrero said he didn't regret the comments and also hinted that he wasn't 100% healthy this year, but denied he had any major injuries.
The reality of the Blue Jays is that they bet on the 27-year-old Guerrero being a franchise-defining talent well into his 30s. It seemed like a reasonable goal when he slashed a monster .397/.494/.795 in last year's postseason, but now he and several of his teammates are underperforming relative to the incredible bar they set last October.
Guerrero tried to get around that awkwardness by suggesting an alternative way for contracts to be evaluated, but he's still got reality in front of him. The Blue Jays simply need him to get better, immediately.
The good news is that 2026 is only a single season, and he has bounced back from down years before. There are still things he does quite well, but he badly needs to rework an approach that has left him wanting for quality contact.

BALTIMORE -- It takes a lot for the Blue Jays’ 2026 elimination to dip below being the story of the day, but that’s exactly what happened Wednesday in Baltimore, as Vladimir Guerrero Jr. addressed some controversial quotes from a recent Spanish-language interview.
In a conversation recently with Veronica Batista, Guerrero addressed his disappointing season and spoke about his 14-year, $500 million extension. Those comments didn’t sit well with fans, though, when Guerrero spoke about being paid for what he’s done for the Blue Jays in the past, not what he’s expected to do in the future.
“I want people to understand one thing,” Guerrero said in Spanish. “The money they gave me wasn’t for what I’m going to do. It was for what I already did. They didn’t pay me because I’m going to hit 40 every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished. People are confused about that, but I think the same way they do. Like, sometimes I even say to myself: bro, they gave you all that money and you’re out here doing nothing. I try.”
Asked about those comments following the Blue Jays being mathematically eliminated from the playoffs Wednesday afternoon, Guerrero stood by them.
"No, I don't regret myself. I'm not lying with what I say,” Guerrero said through interpreter Hector Lebron. “I understand some fans, they don't understand the way and what I was trying to say specifically, but what I said is the way I feel."
This takes us back to the lessons learned in Spring Training of 2025, when Guerrero and the Blue Jays were first negotiating his $500 million extension.
Every few days, another Spanish-language podcast or television appearance featuring Guerrero would be released, often with journalists or interviewers from his native Dominican Republic. It’s important to ensure that nothing is lost in translation, first and foremost, then to contextualize when and why these things were said.
Last spring, for example, a couple of those interviews lingered for weeks at a time before being posted, which stirred up more discourse than anyone -- perhaps even Guerrero -- had planned.
This time, Guerrero’s comments days later seemed to line up with his initial interview with Batista, which was making its rounds on social media throughout Wednesday’s Game 1 of the doubleheader. At one point, Guerrero was also asked to expand on those comments and explain why he was thinking that.
“That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year. I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn’t help my team get to the postseason,” Guerrero said. “I said I felt -- that it’s my personal opinion -- that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.”
Getting Guerrero right is the Blue Jays’ No. 1 priority this offseason. It might be No. 2 and No. 3, as well. If he’s hitting 40-plus home runs, then the Blue Jays might have more of an appetite for moments like this, but it lands at a particularly rough time, given the season he’s just had. Guerrero has hit just nine home runs this season with an OPS that’s been hovering below .700.
“He’s got all the potential in the world. We know that. We’ve seen him be one of, if not the best, players in the game,” John Schneider said. “Years like this, they can happen. Myself, the staff and Vlad, he’s not chalking this one up to ‘one of those years.’ He worked tirelessly to get out of the funk he was in. He tried new things. He tried different ways to prepare and he posted every single day. Definitely not what we expected, what he expected. It’s not what we expect out of him going forward and not what he expects out of himself going forward.”

The Toronto Blue Jays began a series with the Baltimore Orioles on Monday, dropping the opener 4-3.
Yet, Tuesday's game was postponed, setting up Wednesday for a doubleheader with the first game scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET.
Ahead of the matchup, Blue Jays manager John Schneider decided to keep his starting lineup relatively similar to Monday's as superstar Vladimir Guerrero Jr. misses his second straight game after exiting Sunday's contest with lower back tightness.
Blue Jays Announce George Springer Decision
While he's been in more of a platoon role this season for Toronto, Schneider is keeping Springer in the cleanup spot for Wednesday's game as he's once again slotted in as the designated hitter.
Across four at-bats on Monday, Springer recorded two hits and an RBI. He'll hit behind Kazuma Okamoto, Josh Smith, and Nathan Lukes, who will man the top three spots in the batting order, while Sean Keys takes over at first base for Guerrero Jr. and hits fifth.
Here's the full Blue Jays lineup:

Springer's 2026 Season
In his 13th MLB season, Springer has had to take a step back in certain ways, most notably defensively, as he hardly plays the outfield anymore for Toronto.
But he still remains a highly productive player at the plate.
Appearing in 123 games for the Blue Jays this season, Springer enters Wednesday hitting .251 with 57 runs, 113 hits, 15 home runs, and 54 RBIs while slugging .408 with a .732 OPS.
Looking at the Blue Jays
At 77-80 overall, one loss would eliminate the Blue Jays from the playoff race, less than a year removed from reaching the World Series.
It's been an underwhelming season for Toronto. And as they sit 4.0 games back of the final Wild Card spot, it's likely they won't be playing in October this year barring a late-season miracle with five regular-season games remaining.

The Toronto Blue Jays are in the middle of a three-game series against the Baltimore Orioles.
The Orioles won the first game of the series 4-3 on Monday. Game 2 was postponed due to inclement weather, and the series will finish with a doubleheader on Wednesday.
The first game of the doubleheader is scheduled to start at 1:35 p.m. EDT. The second game will begin at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Blue Jays announced their lineup for the first game of the doubleheader, and it includes a notable decision involving Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
Toronto Blue Jays Make Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Decision Amid Orioles Series
Guerrero is out of the lineup for the second straight game for the first game of the doubleheader on Wednesday.
The first baseman was removed from Sunday’s win over the Texas Rangers with lower back tightness, according to MLB.com’s Keegan Matheson.
Update: Guerrero is now IN the lineup.
Here is Toronto’s lineup for Wednesday afternoon’s game:
- Nathan Lukes RF
- Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 1B
- Kazuma Okamoto 3B
- George Springer DH
- Josh Smith LF
- Andres Gimenez SS
- Brandon Valenzuela C
- Myles Straw CF
- Ernie Clement 2B
SP: RHP Max Scherzer (3-8, 6.07 ERA, 54 SO)
Here is the Orioles’ lineup:
- Dylan Beavers LF
- Pete Alonso 1B
- Gunnar Henderson SS
- Coby Mayo DH
- Edwin Encarnacion-Strand 3B
- Colton Cowser CF
- Jeremiah Jackson 2B
- Leody Taveras RF
- Carlos Narvaez C
SP: RHP Chris Bassitt (8-5, 4.64 ERA, 72 SO)
Looking at Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s Season
Guerrero has easily had the worst season of his career, posting 1.2 fWAR and a 97 wRC+ with just nine home runs and 56 RBI over 141 games.
In Guerrero’s defense, he has dealt with numerous injuries this year that he played through. His back has bothered him much of the season, and he also dealt with a hamstring issue earlier this season. Not to mention, he missed games with a concussion.
Since making his MLB debut in 2019, Guerrero has posted 21.8 fWAR and a 132 wRC+ with 192 home runs and 647 RBI. The first baseman signed a 14-year, $500 million contract extension with Toronto in spring 2025.
Toronto Blue Jays Right Now
One year after making it to the World Series, Toronto has a 77-80 record.
The Blue Jays haven’t been officially eliminated yet, but just one more loss from the club will seal their fate.
Even if they win out, they’d need a ton of help from around the league to sneak into the playoffs.

Sep 23, 2026, 11:45 AM ET
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (back) remains out of action for Game 1 of Wednesday's doubleheader at Camden Yards against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles, per MLB.com. Sean Keys will make another start at first base and will bat fifth against Orioles right-hander Chris Bassitt. Guerrero is considered day-to-day right now in the final week of the regular season after departing Sunday's game early against the Texas Rangers due to tightness in his lower back. It is something that the 27-year-old Canadian slugger has already dealt with this year, and it could explain why the six-time All-Star has had a very disappointing 2026 campaign. Guerrero enters play on Wednesday with a .263/.336/.359 slash line, a .695 OPS, only nine home runs, 56 RBI, 71 runs scored, and seven steals across his 529 at-bats. Toronto entered play on Wednesday four games out of the final wild-card spot in the American League and on the brink of elimination. If they lose the first game of Wednesday's doubleheader, Guerrero could be shut down for the rest of the week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com

Jeremy Pena Suffers Wrist Injury on Tuesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 23, 2026, 11:38 AM ET
Houston Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena (wrist) was hit on the right wrist with a 96.4 mph sinker in Tuesday's game against the Seattle Mariners and was removed in the eighth inning, according to Chandler Rome of The Athletic. Pena attempted to stay in the contest, but he was eventually replaced by Nick Allen at shortstop after going 1-for-4 at the plate with two runs scored and two strikeouts. The Astros likely sent Pena for X-rays, and we will pass along the results when we have them. Fantasy managers will want to check back later to see if the Astros' starting shortstop will be available for Wednesday's game in Seattle against the Mariners. Losing Pena for the rest of the final week of the 2026 regular season would be a huge blow, with the Astros going into Wednesday's action tied for first in the American League West with the Texas Rangers. The 29-year-old Pena has missed time this year due to various injuries, but he has been solid when healthy, slashing .275/.325/.469 with a .795 OPS, 20 home runs, 51 RBI, 77 runs scored, and 10 stolen bases in 107 games across 461 plate appearances.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Chandler Rome
Ceddanne Rafaela Set to Return From Injured List on Wednesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 11:08 PM ET
The Boston Red Sox plan to activate second baseman/outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela (quadriceps) from the 10-day injured list on Wednesday, manager Chad Tracy told Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. Rafaela should be back in the starting lineup for Boston in Game 2 of the series against the Cleveland Guardians. He has been out since Sept. 6 with a strained right quad but did not play in a minor-league rehab game. The 26-year-old continues to contribute across most fantasy baseball categories, but he could be a little rusty upon his return to the big leagues as the Red Sox try to get him going again before the wild-card series against the division-rival New York Yankees begins next week. Rafaela made the All-Star team for the first time in his career in 2026 and will return to a nice .282/.317/.443 slash line, a career-high .760 OPS, 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 17 stolen bases, and 67 runs scored across 135 games played. If Rafaela hits a home run by the end of the weekend, he will have a new career high in home runs in his fourth year in the majors.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Sep 22, 2026, 11:00 PM ET
Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell said that third baseman Alex Bregman (face) will not be placed on the injured list and could return to the team's lineup before the end of the regular season, per Russell Dorsey of Yahoo Sports. Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle during Chicago's game against the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday. The 32-year-old suffered multiple facial fractures, but he was able to avoid surgery and appears to be on track to return to the Cubs for the postseason. Across 693 plate appearances in 2026, Bregman is hitting .262/.352/.452 with 26 home runs, 89 RBI, 89 runs scored, and three stolen bases. He's been one of the best hitters in baseball in the second half of the season, hitting .296 with 17 home runs across 262 plate appearances since the All-Star break. With Bregman in the middle of it, the Cubs lineup profiles as arguably the best in MLB in 2026.--Will Brady
Source: Yahoo Sports - Russell Dorsey
Sep 22, 2026, 10:52 PM ET
Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said that closer Aroldis Chapman (lat) "should be cleared in the next day or two," per Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. Chapman has not pitched since September 13 due to lat tightness, but it appears as though the 38-year-old is on the doorstep of a return to his role in the ninth inning for the Red Sox. Across 50 2/3 innings (52 games) in 2026, Chapman has recorded a 1.95 ERA and 1.14 WHIP with 68 strikeouts and 34 saves. The veteran left-hander has not been quite as dominant as he was in his first season with Boston in 2025, but he's still posted an excellent 32.4% strikeout rate and blown just two save chances. When healthy, Chapman remains a must-start closer for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey

Sep 22, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Texas Rangers designated hitter Joc Pederson (hand) has been placed on the 10-day injured list (retroactive to September 19) due to a fracture in his left hand. The 34-year-old had been attempting to play through the injury, but it appears that he and the team ultimately came to the conclusion that a trip to the IL was necessary. Pederson bounced back from a brutal 2025 campaign with a solid year at the plate in 2026, hitting .235/.329/.487 with 26 home runs, 53 RBI, 56 runs scored, and two stolen bases. The veteran lefty slugger re-established himself as an excellent source of big-side platoon power, posting an 11.2% barrel rate and a 50.7% hard-hit rate. With Pederson now sidelined through at least the remainder of the regular season, Texas has rotated shortstop Corey Seager and backup catcher Elias Diaz through its DH spot.--Will Brady

Landen Roupp Shut Down for Remainder of 2026


Will Brady




Sep 22, 2026, 10:34 PM ET
San Francisco Giants starting pitcher Landen Roupp told reporters on Tuesday that his 2026 season is over, per Justice delos Santos of The Mercury News. Per delos Santos, Roupp feels fine physically, but is being shut down because he has already blown past his previous career high in innings pitched. Across 155 innings (29 starts) this year, the 28-year-old recorded a 9-14 record with a 4.01 ERA, 1.30 WHIP, and 143 strikeouts. Roupp limits power (0.64 HR/9), which has helped him develop into a capable innings eater for fantasy managers. However, the right-hander's production upside is limited by his middling strikeout rate (21.8%) and his poor walk rate (11.4%). Between his penchant for allowing walks and generating ground balls, Roupp is unlikely to be an asset in the WHIP category without a change in his approach on the mound.--Will Brady
Source: The Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Sep 22, 2026, 10:29 PM ET
Seattle Mariners closer Andres Munoz (knee) "should be ok" and could be available to his team on Tuesday night after undergoing an MRI on his injured knee, per Shannon Drayer of Seattle Sports 710. Munoz was pulled from his most recent appearance on Sunday after tweaking his right knee, but he appears to have avoided serious injury. It's been a disappointing year overall for the 27-year-old, who has recorded a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, 89 strikeouts, and 28 saves across 57 1/3 innings (61 games). Munoz has struggled with home runs (1.41 HR/9) and has blown a career-high 10 saves. However, the hard-throwing right-hander is still averaging 99.7 miles per hour on his fastball and has logged an elite 37.1% strikeout rate. Heading into 2027, Munoz could be an excellent buy-low candidate for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: Seattle Sports 710 - Shannon Drayer
Sep 22, 2026, 10:22 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell (groin) is scheduled to start against the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, per David Vassegh of AM 570 LA Sports. Snell exited early from his most recent start on September 16 due to a groin issue. However, it appears that Snell will be able to make one final start before the postseason. It's been a lost season due to injury for the 33-year-old, who has missed time due to elbow and shoulder troubles. Still, Snell has been effective when healthy, recording a 4-1 record with a 1.86 ERA, 1.09 WHIP, and 52 strikeouts across 38 2/3 innings (eight starts). Fantasy managers may be able to get one more solid outing from Snell on Saturday, but the Dodgers also have little incentive to push his pitch count deep into the game.--Will Brady

Sep 22, 2026, 10:11 PM ET
Atlanta Braves outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. (shin) exited early from his team's 4-0 loss to the Cincinnati Reds on Tuesday after fouling a ball off his leg. Per Mark Bowman of MLB.com, X-rays on the leg were negative, and the star outfielder is now being listed as day-to-day with a shin contusion. Acuna Jr. was hitless in one plate appearance before leaving the game. While it appears that he's avoided a serious injury, Atlanta could still choose to be extremely cautious with Acuna Jr. in the final week of the regular season. The Braves have already clinched the National League East title and are likely locked into the number three seed in the NL. Across 455 plate appearances in 2026, Acuna Jr. is hitting .259/.352/.462 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 60 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. If he misses any time, Braves outfielders Brewer Hicklen and Mike Yastrzemski would likely see an increase in at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: MLB.com - Mark Bowman
Shohei Ohtani Expected to Return on Wednesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 7:50 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani (knee) is expected to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday, as had been the hope, manager Dave Roberts told Sonja Chen of MLB.com. Ohtani is getting ready to return from a stay on the IL that lasted for several weeks. The four-time MVP has not made a start as a pitcher since July 3 against the Padres, and he is not expected to be an option on the mound for the Dodgers at all the rest of the regular season or postseason. But Roberts expects Ohtani to be ready to return on Wednesday against San Diego as the team's primary designated hitter. They will want the 32-year-old Japanese superstar to get some live at-bats going into the final weekend of the regular season before the playoffs begin in October. Ohtani's two-way status has taken a toll on him physically in 2026, although he still has hit a strong .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, 11 stolen bases, and 89 runs scored in 130 games. While he probably will not win a fourth straight MVP award, Ohtani can definitely still help the Dodgers win an unprecedented third straight World Series title if he is past his knee and biceps injuries that have bothered him for around half the season.--Keith Hernandez

Kyle Tucker Back in Action Tuesday Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Sep 22, 2026, 7:44 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker (knee, shin) is starting in right field and is hitting fifth for Tuesday's series opener against the division-rival San Diego Padres and right-hander Michael King, per MLB.com. Tucker was held out of the series finale on Sunday against the division-rival San Francisco Giants with a minor knee/shin injury, but he is ready for this week in a crucial series at Dodger Stadium. The 29-year-old lefty slugger has not had the first season in L.A. that he envisioned, and he enters Tuesday's action with a .234/.334/.393 slash line, a .727 OPS, 17 home runs, 70 RBI, 88 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases across 148 games and 602 plate appearances. Tucker has hit .283 (17-for-60) with a 1.059 OPS, six homers, and 13 RBI in 19 games in September. Against King in 12 career at-bats, he is hitting .083 with one RBI.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Xavier Edwards Still Sidelined Against Cubs


Keith Hernandez

Miami Marlins middle infielder Xavier Edwards (thumb) remains out of action for Tuesday's series opener at Wrigley Field against the Chicago Cubs, according to MLB.com. Jared Serna will make the start at the keystone for the Fish on Tuesday and will bat ninth against Cubs left-hander Shota Imanaga. Edwards is missing a second straight start after he injured his thumb on Saturday in San Diego against the Padres. The Marlins are eliminated from postseason contention, but the hope is that Edwards will be able to return during the final week of the 2026 regular season. In his fourth season in the big leagues with the Marlins, the 27-year-old has had another strong season, hitting .280/.360/.371 with a .730 OPS, a career-high six home runs, 52 RBI, 21 stolen bases, and 61 runs scored in 142 games played and 595 plate appearances. Injuries have started to take a toll on the Toronto Blue Jays lately. While it seemed like there was still hope for Toronto to make the postseason a couple of weeks ago, that has ultimately not turned out to be the case.
The struggles have been real, and the injuries have not made it easier. Outfielder Brett Bateman suffered a hip injury on Monday night, while first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has dealt with back tightness. Not to mention starter Trey Yesavage, who just returned from knee surgery after six weeks.
Ace Dylan Cease had been holding down the rotation recently, but even he hasn't been immune to the injury bug that has hurt the Blue Jays this season. Cease has been a lifeline to Toronto's pitching staff, but had been dealing with shoulder fatigue over the past few weeks, according to manager John Schneider.
Cease struggled mightily against the Texas Rangers on Friday, going just 2.2 innings and walking six, while giving up four runs (one earned). He went back to Toronto for an MRI and was scratched from his next start on Wednesday.
It was revealed on Monday that the MRI only showed inflammation in the right shoulder and no structural issues. Cease will not need surgery for anything more serious.
More on Cease's Injury Situation
The 30-year-old explained the news himself and the fact that he's just been diagnosed with shoulder inflammation. This isn't an issue that is expected to go into 2027 and affect his availability for next season.
It's still unlikely that Cease ends up pitching again this season with less than a week left, although that's still being determined. Given the Jays are basically out of postseason contention, there's really no need to push him.
The shoulder issue is what caused Cease's pitch velocity to go down.
“The velocity being down has been a little bit concerning,” Cease said, according to Keegan Matheson of MLB.com. "But at the same time, I’m getting outs. It wasn’t anything that was too scary because nothing about it feels like I’ve got something that needs surgery."
After his incredible complete game at the Boston Red Sox on July 25, where he threw 120 pitches, Cease didn't look as strong, even though he still ended up throwing six quality starts from that time until now.
“It’s definitely a bit heavy and achy, just not normal,” Cease said. "The last couple of starts, the velo keeps going down and down. Especially that last one, I almost felt like I was hurting the team."
It's clear that the issue caught him to him, but the fact that he pitched through it at a high level for some time shows the quality of Cease.
He has posted a 2.40 ERA in 29 starts, which is the second-lowest mark in the American League. Cease has a career-high 239 strikeouts in 169 innings pitched, with an 11-6 record.

item.content:encoded:
El primera base dominicano de los Azulejos de Toronto, Vladimir Guerrero Jr., quedó fuera de la alineación para el primero de la serie ante los Orioles de Baltimore —encuentro que terminó en derrota por pizarra de 4-3 el lunes en Camden Yards—, al experimentar tensión en la parte inferior de la espalda.
Lee también: Eduardo Valencia deja buenas sensaciones en su primer año
El infielder ha lidiado con molestias en la espalda durante toda la temporada, las cuales ha superado al punto de seguir activo; sin embargo, la dolencia se agravó hace varios días cuando se estiró para completar una jugada en la inicial. Además, el domingo escaló hasta afectar su swing lo suficiente como para que el equipo lo retirara del último de la serie ante los Rangers de Texas en la parte baja del cuarto episodio.
Tras la derrota en Baltimore, los Azulejos se alejaron a tres juegos y medio del tercer comodín de la Liga Americana, ocupado por los Medias Blancas de Chicago, equipo que de paso posee el desempate a su favor. Este panorama complica aún más las remotas esperanzas del conjunto canadiense de avanzar a la postemporada.
Se nota al hacer swing
Pese a la situación, el mánager de los Azulejos, John Schneider, espera que su pupilo regrese pronto a la alineación, independientemente del contexto de la lucha por un comodín. «Siempre y cuando se sienta mejor y no esté realmente incómodo al batear», dijo el timonel, quien añadió que el estatus del jugador «realmente es día a día».
En ese sentido, el estratega de 46 años explicó el origen de la molestia: «Ocurre más cuando está aterrizando y rotando. Podías verlo en algunos de sus swings ayer. Sabíamos desde el principio que estaba un poco tenso, pero no estaba realmente logrando su swing habitual».
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. podría tener algo de tiempo para recuperarse, sobre todo si los pronósticos de lluvia trastocan los juegos del martes y el miércoles, previo a la última serie de los Azulejos en casa ante los Rojos de Cincinnati.

Arenado also has a favorable schedule in the final week of the regular season, as the Diamondbacks will open a three-game set at Coors Field against the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday. In his first 16 starts over 97 innings this year, Melton had a stingy 1.86 ERA while holding hitters to a .201 average and .607 OPS. But he struggled to close it out over his final three starts before Sunday's abbreviated outing, allowing 13 runs (11 earned), 18 hits, six walks, and three hit batsmen in 13 2/3 innings. When fully healthy, Melton is an intriguing arm for fantasy managers with a legitimate six-pitch mix and precise command of his four-seam fastball, sinker, and cutter.--Keith Hernandez

Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 10:48 AM ET
Detroit Tigers right-handed pitching prospect River Ryan, who was acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in the blockbuster trade involving Tarik Skubal this summer, will make his Tigers debut on Monday and start against the Washington Nationals, according to Jason Beck of MLB.com. item.content:encoded:
According to a prominent Canadian sports writer, Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is “embarrassed” by his poor season.
The six-time MLB All-Star is batting just .262 for the Blue Jays with an OPS of .694 and an OPS+ of 92, indicating his bat has been 8% below league average. He has only hit 9 home runs this season, including just 1 home run at Rogers Centre.
Considering Guerrero makes $40.2 million this season, the first year of a 14-year, $500 million contract, it has been downright shocking, to say the least, to see how poorly he has performed at the plate this year for Toronto, which is likely to miss the postseason after making it all the way to the World Series last year, in what can only be described as a massive fall from grace.
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. ‘Embarrassed’ by Poor Performance
According to Steve Simmons of the Toronto Sun, Guerrero has told those close to him that he is “embarrassed” by his play this season.
“Those who know Guerrero best say he is terribly embarrassed by his lack of production and he has grown tired of all the meetings, the coaching, the daily work, the noise that has not resulted in anything resembling success during this wayward season,” Simmons wrote.
Simmons also provided another interesting note, pointing out that in the event of an MLB lockout — which seems likely at this point — Guerrero will not be able to work with the Blue Jays coaches after December 1 to help get his swing back on track this offseason.
“What complicates the off-season for Guerrero and the Jays is the possibility of a lockout on Dec. 1. If that happens, and the Jays have plans to work with Guerrero to get his swing back, there can be no contact between the player and the team after that date,” Simmons wrote.
Blue Jays Likely to Miss Playoffs
With just six games left this season, the Blue Jays have a 77-79 record, and making the postseason is going to be next to impossible, as the team is currently 3 GB of the Chicago White Sox in the hunt for the third and final American League Wild Card spot.
That’s actually 4 GB, though, because the White Sox hold the tiebreaker over Toronto, so the odds of the Blue Jays making it to the postseason bracket are extremely slim right now.
The only hope Toronto has is that they win their last six games of the season to get to 83-79 and hope that Chicago goes 2-4 in their last six games to finish at 82-80.
Or, the Cleveland Guardians can go 2-4 over their final six games to also finish at 83-79, as Toronto at least has the tiebreaker over Cleveland.
With that in mind, math is not on the Blue Jays’ side right now, as time is running out this season and there simply aren’t enough games left for Toronto to get into the postseason bracket.
And fairly or unfairly, since it is a team sport, Guerrero’s bad season with the bat is a big reason why the team isn’t going anywhere this year.

item.content:encoded:
One well-timed hot streak from a star player can be all a team needs to go on a big run.
While many key contributors struggled in the first half of 2026, several have picked it up big time since the All-Star break, lifting their clubs to late-season success.
Here are 10 players -- five hitters and five pitchers -- who have turned things around in the second half.
All stats are through Saturday's games unless otherwise specified.
Hitters
Alex Bregman, Cubs
For as good as National League MVP Award favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong has been lately, it’s actually Bregman who entered Saturday leading all qualifying hitters with a 168 wRC+ in the second half. The third baseman has a .298/.376/.609 slash line since the All-Star break, with his 17 second-half homers tied for fourth most in MLB.
Batting just .241 with nine home runs and a .695 OPS prior to the break, Bregman hadn’t exactly been meeting expectations after signing a five-year, $175 million deal with the Cubs. Now, though, he is up to 5.1 FanGraphs WAR, his highest total since 2022 (5.4). He’s been a big reason the Cubs are currently on track to host an NL Wild Card Series at Wrigley Field, and he will be a key bat in the middle of Chicago’s lineup in the postseason.
Steven Kwan, Guardians
With this week’s series win over the White Sox, the Guardians have surged into first place in the AL Central, in large part thanks to their leadoff hitter’s resurgence. In addition to his strong defense in left field -- Kwan has won four straight AL Gold Gloves in left to begin his career -- Kwan has been on fire at the plate.
After a disappointing first-half slash line of .225/.332/.282, including a .188 batting average in May, Kwan ranks second among qualifiers with a .347 average and is tied with Yordan Alvarez for first with a .435 on-base percentage in the second half. He has been setting the table admirably for a Cleveland club not getting as much as usual from third baseman José Ramírez (94 wRC+) and could help the Guardians secure not only the division title but a key first-round bye.
Jackson Merrill, Padres
Merrill took a step back in 2025 after finishing second to the Pirates’ Paul Skenes in 2024 NL Rookie of the Year Award voting, and the Padres center fielder appeared headed for further regression based on early returns in 2026. Merrill’s OPS was below .600 in late May as San Diego scuffled offensively, and he took a .219/.278/.350 slash line into the break.
Since then, Merrill has been a major reason why the Padres have a 38-21 (.644) record in the second half, tied with the Brewers for the best in the NL. He’s hitting .312 with 16 home runs, 48 RBIs and a .944 OPS in 59 games in the second half while playing standout defense in center. Merrill’s ability to recapture his rookie form has given the Padres a fighting chance to host a Wild Card Series, and he’ll be a key middle-of-the-order bat for the club.
George Springer, Blue Jays
Springer improved his OPS by nearly 300 points from 2024 to 2025, slashing .309/.399/.560 and finishing seventh in AL MVP balloting as Toronto fell just short of a World Series title. But the veteran’s numbers fell off again early in 2026, especially after Springer returned from a stint on the injured list for a left big toe fracture. He hit just .218 with a .677 OPS before the All-Star break, a period of rest that seemed to help considerably.
Springer recorded multiple hits in five of his first nine second-half games, finishing July with an .878 OPS, before batting .321 with an .858 OPS in August. While he has slowed a bit in September, battling multiple injuries, he has clearly found his footing at the plate. It might not be enough to drag a Blue Jays team dealing with a host of pitching injuries and a down year from Vladimir Guerrero Jr. to the postseason, but Toronto -- three games out of an AL Wild Card spot -- still has a chance.
Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres
While Merrill’s turnaround has been integral to the Padres’ second-half surge, Tatis’ production out of the leadoff spot has perhaps been even more important. The three-time All-Star began the season by scorching the baseball into the ground, going 55 games before hitting his first home run of the year on May 30.
The second half brought on a true power surge for Tatis, who homered three times in his first four games after the All-Star break and is now up to 24 dingers on the season. Entering Saturday, his 167 wRC+ in the second half was second in MLB, behind only Bregman. Tatis has raised his season OPS to .819 and has given the Padres a dangerous option at leadoff down the stretch.
Pitchers
Brayan Bello, Red Sox
Bello has turned the page on a dismal start to the season. The right-hander, coming off a 3.35 ERA as a starter in 2025, had a 9.00 ERA in his first six starts of 2026 and was moved to a bulk-relief role. Still, Bello took a 6.06 ERA into the All-Star break as the Red Sox finally began to heat up, winning nine straight games to end the first half and extending the streak to a franchise record-tying 15.
Bello has continued to impress for Boston, earning the start on Saturday and baffling the Rays over eight innings of one-run ball with 11 strikeouts. In the midst of a statistically unprecedented season, he’s found something that works, which has been crucial for a Red Sox team that has surged into postseason position and appears headed for another clash with the Yankees in the AL Wild Card Series.
Robert Gasser, Brewers
Tommy John surgery in June 2024 cut short Gasser’s promising rookie season, but he returned to make two solid starts at the tail end of 2025. The left-hander couldn’t sustain that success early in 2026, taking a 5.24 ERA into the All-Star break after being tagged for seven runs in three innings in his final first-half start.
Since then, Gasser has a 3.00 ERA in 57 innings of work after holding the Orioles scoreless over seven excellent innings on Saturday in Baltimore. In his first four September outings, including two against the Cubs, he has allowed just four earned runs across 21 innings pitched. With Brandon Woodruff’s 2026 return questionable and Kyle Harrison struggling mightily, Gasser’s improvement has made him an important arm for a Milwaukee team fighting to secure the NL’s No. 1 seed.
Tyler Mahle, Braves
Mahle owned a 5.13 ERA through his first 18 starts of 2026 for the Giants, but the Braves saw something in the veteran right-hander. Atlanta acquired Mahle ahead of the Trade Deadline for righty reliever Anthony Molina in a move that has paid considerable dividends for the Braves’ battered rotation.
Mahle has allowed only seven earned runs in eight starts for Atlanta, completing six or more innings in all but one of those outings. His 1.28 ERA in that span is the third best among all pitchers (min. 40 innings), and he’s been an excellent complement to ace lefty Chris Sale atop the Braves rotation. With Spencer Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach, Bryce Elder, Reynaldo López and Hurston Waldrep all on the injured list, Mahle has not only covered important innings but has been remarkably effective.
Aaron Nola, Phillies
Nola had an ERA above 6 in an injury-marred 2025 season, and his 2026 looked to be more of the same. The usually dependable right-hander gave up 20 home runs in the first half alone, tied for the fifth most in MLB, and headed into the All-Star break with a 5.75 ERA.
Since then, Nola has returned to near-vintage form for the Phillies, who have also gotten strong second halves from lefty Jesús Luzardo (currently on the injured list with left shoulder inflammation) and rookie righty Andrew Painter. After Thursday’s excellent start against the Mets, Nola has a 2.78 ERA in the second half, striking out 67 in 71 1/3 innings despite giving up 14 more home runs in just 12 starts. If he can limit the long balls, he could be at least an adequate replacement for Luzardo if the southpaw cannot return for the start of the postseason.
Brandon Pfaadt, D-backs
Pfaadt hasn’t quite lived up to his billing as a former top prospect just yet, but he’s shown flashes, such as his success against the Dodgers and Phillies during the D-backs’ 2023 World Series run. The righty's recent results have been quite encouraging, too: Pfaadt has a 3.01 ERA in the second half, including a run of 27 2/3 scoreless innings across four starts from July 28-Aug. 14. 
Optioned to Triple-A Reno in June after a poor start to the year, Pfaadt now has the chance to help pitch the D-backs into the playoffs, which might be difficult in an NL Wild Card race featuring the Cubs, Phillies and Padres. Pfaadt is lined up to start during Arizona’s final series of the season, a pivotal three-game set in San Diego from Sept. 25-27, and his outing could determine the D-backs’ postseason fate.

“La Bestia with Ronald Acuña Jr.” is the first show from a new partnership with Rimas Sports in which the Puerto Rican sports agency will co-produce original podcasts and content with iHeartMedia’s My Cultura network. Rimas Sports and iHeartMedia are both committed to building and celebrating the next generation of Latino voices.

item.content:encoded:
Many fans rely on numbers to tell the story of a baseball season. For 2026, I’m going with letters. Here’s the story of the regular season from A to Z.

A: Yordan Alvarez: He’s the only qualifier in baseball with an OBP of over .400. He’s leading the American League in batting, on-base, slugging, OPS, and walks. Where would Joe Espada’s Astros be without him? Yordan is still the favorite to win the American League MVP, despite his numbers falling off a bit down the stretch.
B: Bryan Baker: Tampa Bay scored 698 runs and allowed 618 in games through September 17. That would give them a record of 84-68 according to the Pythagorean Theorem. But they were 93-59, nine games better. Credit in part goes to their closer Baker, leading the league with 40 saves this season..
C: Pete Crow-Armstrong: When the Cubs suffered through a 10-game losing streak in May, Pete batted just .161 (5-36 AB) in those 10 games. In games through September 17, PCA in 85 Cubs victories: .357/.442/.740. He scored 89 runs in 85 Cubs wins. The NL MVP by a mile. You cannot tell the story of the 2026 season without talking about Pete Crow-Armstrong.
D: Jacob deGrom: On September 10, deGrom started against the Mariners in Seattle. In six innings, he faced just 19 batters, one over the minimum. He struck out 12, gave up one hit, walked none, and didn’t allow a run. He left the game with Texas leading by three runs. The bullpen flushed away the lead and Texas wound up losing the game. The story of deGrom’s career. Jacob is historically significant. He has started 277 games in his career, and three of his top 10 (ranked by Pitchers’ Game Score) have come in 2026.
E: Errors: There’s only been one season EVER with fewer errors per game than 2026. Of course, that would be 2025. No pitcher has made more than four errors this season. In 1969, Jim Kaat won a Gold Glove, despite making eight errors (tied for the MLB lead with Boston’s Ray Culp among pitchers). Gold Gloves were all reputation in those days. In fact, Kaat’s longtime Minnesota teammate, Zoilo Versalles, won a Gold Glove in 1965 despite making 39 errors!
F: Freddie Freeman: Freeman has hit 32 doubles this year and 579 in his career. Is 579 doubles a lot? Well, that’s 90 more than the next-closest active player, Paul Goldschmidt. And when Freddie legs out his 600th, he’ll become only the 19th player with at least 600 doubles. He’s a little more than a season away from passing both Hank Aaron (624) and Barry Bonds (601).
G: Vladimir Guerrero Jr.: Vlad Jr. hit a home run every 25 at-bats in 2025. He’s hit a home run every 58 at-bats in 2026. He didn’t hit his first home run at home this year until Toronto’s 75th home game. He had gone 84 straight home games without a homer.
H: Bryce Harper: In March, Harper hit a two-run game-tying homer in the 8th inning of the WBC Finals. This season, his wRC+ (139) has been one of the top dozen in the majors. In October, can he lead the Phillies to his first World Series championship?
I: Raisel Iglesias: The Braves have spent all season in first place, and Iglesias is a big part of that. In the last 10 years (2017-2026) only one player (Kenley Jansen) has more saves than Iglesias. He’s 33-for-36 in save chances this year for the Braves. But here’s the thing: over the last five years, he’s saved 130 games for the Braves, but only one in the postseason. That has to change.
J: Aaron Judge: #99 missed 99 days (84 games) this season with a rib injury, but the three-time MVP came back in mid-September with enough time to get his timing back at the plate. Yankees fans will have to hope that the leg tightness isn’t a big deal.
K: Steven Kwan: There hasn’t been a hotter hitter in the American League since the start of July. Kwan is batting .350 since July 1, and .351 since the All-Star break. The Guardians have needed every bit of his offense, as José Ramírez has not been the same since returning from his broken left hamate bone.
L: Brandon Lowe: In his first season with Pittsburgh, Lowe has hit a career best 30 homers and has an OPS over .800. The Pirates offense was one of the big stories of the first half of the 2026 season, and Lowe was a big reason why. In the second half, injuries to Oneil Cruz and Ryan O’Hearn have sunk the Bucs but the offense was fun while it lasted.
M: Jacob Misiorowski: Milwaukee has the best record in baseball, and he’s a big reason why. Has any Brewers pitcher ever had a better season than the 24-year-old ace? Sorry, fans of Teddy Higuera. The answer is no. “The Miz” leads the majors in strikeouts (243). He leads the majors in ERA (1.89). He’s striking out more than 13 batters per nine innings! Misiorowski has had 1,053 pitches this season over 100.0 mph. No one else in pitch tracking era (2008-present) has had a season of 1,000 or more.
N: No-Hitters: On May 25, three Astros pitchers Tatsuya Imai (6 IP), Steven Okert (1 IP), and Alimber Santa (2 IP) combined to complete the Astros’ fifth combined no-hitter in franchise history. No one pitcher has completed a no-hitter since Blake Snell did it in August of 2024 for the Giants.
O: Shohei Ohtani: There are two players whose last name starts with “O” with more homers than Ohtani this season: Matt Olson and Kazuma Okamoto. But Ohtani made 14 brilliant starts (1.79 ERA) and his wRC+ of 142 is in the top 10 in the game.
P: Salvador Perez: The 36-year-old put up nearly 600 at-bats this season. And while most of them came as a DH or 1B, he did start 44 games behind the plate. In his 15-year career, he’s caught 1,427 games (1,396 starts) and nearly 12,000 innings.
Q: Quick games: On September 7, in an afternoon game at Citizens Bank Park, the Phillies beat the Braves 1-0 in a game that took 1:51 to play. On June 16 at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers defeated the Rays 1-0 in a game that took 1:52 to complete. And in early April, the Royals defeated the White Sox in games on April 10 and 11 that lasted in 1:54 and 1:55, respectively. Thank you, pitch clock.
R: Eduardo Rodriguez: The Diamondbacks have won 22 of E-Rod’s first 30 starts. Talk about valuable! He has a 2.62 ERA this season (it was 5.04 and 5.02 in the two previous seasons). This is his best year since 2019.
S: Cam Schlittler: Is he the AL MVP, or just the AL Cy Young? The Yankees won 20 of his 31 starts. The Yankees don’t need a lot of offense when he takes the mound. He has a 1.14 ERA in 16 road starts this season! Since earned runs became official in both leagues in 1913, Schlittler’s 1.14 road ERA is the fourth best (minimum 15 road starts). The top three: Bob Gibson in 1968 (0.81 ERA); Walter Johnson in 1913 (1.06 ERA); and Greg Maddux in 1995 (1.12 ERA).
T: Bruce Turang: What a player! His OPS has gone up in each of his first four seasons. He’s now a 20 HR/20 SB/100 runs/100 RBI player. The Brewers need him to improve his performance in last year’s NLCS vs. the Dodgers, when he went 1-for-15 (.067).
U: Uncle Charlie (curveball): The curveball is heading toward extinction, much like individual no-hitters. Curveballs have only accounted for 6.4% of pitches this season, the second lowest rate since first tracked in 2008 (2024: 6.1%). That’s pure curves, not including slow curves or knuckle-curves. Want to know which pitcher has thrown the most curveballs (including knuckle and slow curves) this year? Philadelphia’s Aaron Nola, at 942.
V: Miguel Vargas: The White Sox have been one of the best stories this year, and we could have given the “V” to manager Max Venable. But Vargas’ 31 home runs and stealing 19 bases in 21 attempts makes him the choice. Vargas has a 4.7 WAR this season, up from 1.9 last year.
W: Willson and Wilyer, the heart of the Boston lineup. Right fielder Wilyer Abreu leads the American League with 36 doubles. He also leads the AL in outfield assists with 12. Willson Contreras has an OPS of .905, second in AL to Alvarez, even ahead of Rays slugger Junior Caminero. Remember, Boston was 14 games under .500 as late as June 24. And then the season turned around.
X: Xander Bogaerts: The Padres have played well down the stretch and now appear likely to reach the postseason. And X-Man has contributed, stealing 21 bases in 22 attempts this year. It’s no fluke, either. He stole 20 of 22 last season. In his four seasons with the Padres, he has stolen 73 bases in 81 attempts. That’s efficiency.
Y: Yoshinobu Yamamoto: The Dodgers’ Yoshinobu Yamamoto has a 1.98 ERA in 10 starts after the All-Star break. He’s probably the key to the Dodgers’ chances of completing a three-peat. Who can forget what he did last October, when he went 5-1, with a 1.45 ERA in 37.1 postseason innings.
Z: Zack Wheeler: From July 21 through August 24, Wheeler had a stretch of seven starts that saw him give up 26 runs (25 earned) in 31.1 innings (7.18 ERA). He was terrific in the first half and recaptured his form down the stretch. If the Phillies are going to go deep into October, they’ll need Wheeler (and their other two aces) to be at the top of their game.
